title: Upstream reconstruction, runtime and tooling maintenance
summary: Review seven material post-pass changes across reconstruction fidelity, authenticated runtime handoff, mod infrastructure and evidence-preserving tooling.
notes: The CPU audit queue contained zero unresolved source/target CPU areas. No CPU architecture, runtime minimum or hardware profile was inferred. The tracker reviewed primary commits and upstream results but did not compile or execute the upstream projects.

The Bruce Lee acceptance reports 70 reference pages, 1,227 entries, 21 decoded tables and deterministic second-pass linking; these are upstream field-run receipts and do not close the separate npm publication gate. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/4c209ab6e79cbb0a34e3b818bf33d8b6fb92f0ba https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/7a45b671dc7b6efc1f0c6b905e57ae1839a8ce3a https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/9caaff4bf206b429d389fcdf5e94d42919600cd9 v2.1.1 closes the previously open publication gate and reports a real-project field pass covering every script command and MCP tool on VICE 3.10. These are upstream field and regression receipts, not a tracker-side VICE run. identity.narrative: Identity: The primary README identifies REA as a CLI/MCP toolkit connecting agents to native, managed, JavaScript, firmware and runtime analysis providers. Classification: This is generic reverse-engineering tooling with a documented retro-relevant DOS MZ/COM and PC-98 analysis lane; it is not itself a game reconstruction. Source CPU: The DOS guide explicitly imports MZ and COM images with Ghidra language `x86:LE:16:Real Mode`; no broader CPU inventory is inferred into this retro-focused record. Target CPU: REA returns analysis evidence and annotations rather than producing a runnable port or reconstructed binary for a distinct output CPU. Build: The README documents npx/npm setup and CLI/MCP use, while the DOS lane documents real Ghidra verification of 16-bit instructions, calls, decompilation and cleanup. Limitations: REA and Ghidra were not installed or executed in this pass. Runtime profiles: The README gives exact supported Node.js version ranges; the DOS guide states verified Linux x64/macOS arm64 Ghidra/JDK lanes without claiming DOS hardware emulation. AI: Operational AI use is explicit because an agent calls REA through MCP; the reviewed evidence does not establish that AI authored the repository, so no contribution tool labels are asserted. Relationships: REA delegates deep native analysis to existing Hopper, Ghidra or IDA providers and cites separate DX-Ball and Touhou reconstruction case studies without absorbing those projects into this tooling record. Evidence: https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/docs/ghidra-dos.md The reviewed changes extend the existing agent-driven analysis toolkit and its evidence pipeline; they do not establish a new reconstructed subject.

build.narrative: The OVL_0077_275B differential exposed that the original JBE tests CF or ZF: equality is not over capacity. Upstream calibrated the compared operands from the original and added below/equal/above cases, increasing the differential from 46 to 49 cases without changing body bytes, hash, identity or credit. A later documentation ruling grounds one display family's game-state evidence in credited consumers, explicitly not segment co-location; it does not expand the reconstructed binary or establish playability. Limitations: The tracker reviewed primary source and upstream results but did not compile, execute, byte-compare or hardware-test this revision. Upstream models the 311-byte, 145-instruction START.EXE resident routine at 03F1:0000 with a generated full-state C implementation and RETF 0Ah behavior, then composes eight overlay-stub calls into that model. Reported verification covers 56 Unicorn cases with all 145 instruction starts and 8 outcomes, 1,124 composed tile calls, 16 DOSBox-X cases and 11 focused checks. Certain error/random cases remain Unicorn-only because DOSBox-X can hang or reboot; no whole-game or playability inference follows.
